This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton. President Trump says he's setting aside
$25 million to reward people who report fraud. NPR's Emily Fang reports the move comes as
Americans are overwhelmingly concerned with corruption in government. Citing, quote,
trillions of potential corruption in U.S. government, Trump said he was incentivizing
people to turn others in for potential fraud. If you turn somebody in and you, let's say,
report and you find a billion dollars, we are giving a commission to that person of 1 percent.
Standing behind Trump was Vice President J.D. Vance, who has been leading an anti-fraud
task force. The force is mainly focused on investigating Medicaid and social services
in states led by Democratic governors. A recent Fox News poll this week showed nearly 90 percent
of Americans surveyed were concerned about government corruption, even more than the
percentage concerned about the economy. Emily Fang, NPR News, The White House.
A day after President Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu,
Vice President J.D. Vance declined to endorse the embattled leader ahead of key Israeli elections
next week. Vance says he's focused on the American elections. Meanwhile, NPR has learned
that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made a secret visit to Israel to visit Netanyahu yesterday,
as NPR's Daniel Estrin reports. There's been no official comment by the U.S.
or Israel, but a person familiar with the matter speaking on condition of anonymity
said Hegseth met with Netanyahu in Israel. President Trump and Netanyahu have been speaking
publicly, suggesting the possibility of a new strike on Iran. Netanyahu's staff released a
video of him next to fighter jets, where he appears to be speaking on the phone with Trump.
Donald, we have a job to finish. You said it and we'll finish it together.
Israel's military announced it's on the highest state of alert ahead of Israel's elections next
week on Tuesday. Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv. A nonprofit group that documents acts of hate
against Asian Americans says a growing share of these incidents now include threats of deportation.
NPR's Adrian Florido reports. Stop AAPI hate was founded during the COVID pandemic when incidents
of hate speech against Asian Americans surged after President Trump linked the virus to Chinese
people. The organization takes reports from victims. It says a majority of hate acts reported
to it now include some kind of anti-immigrant sentiment. Cynthia Choi co-founded the group.
We see time and time again bad actors mimicking what they've heard from the most powerful person
in this country, Trump. I'm glad Trump is going to deport you or I can't wait to report you to ICE.
Choi says the findings show how high level political rhetoric
trickles down to affect real people's lives. Adrian Florido, NPR News.
Most of the U.S. stock market rose today. The S&P 500 added a quarter percent. This is NPR News.
The U.S. government has certified Boeing's 737 MAX 10 airliner for passenger service after
years of delays. The FAA says production of the largest version of Boeing's best-selling 737
family has been approved after extensive safety reviews and thousands of hours of test flights.
The MAX 10 was introduced in 2017 but faced technical and safety-related concerns that
slowed its certification. Yellowstone National Park in Wyoming received a $105 million donation
yesterday. As Jenna McMurtry reports, it's the biggest financial gift in national park history.
The donor is a Blackstone energy company that operates thousands of miles of pipelines across
the country. The funds are intended to improve access for Wyoming students and the overall
visitor experience. Retired Yellowstone superintendent Dan Wank calls the donation a
"remarkable gift." "Parks across the country are chronically underfunded and that's just not
subject of this administration that's been throughout my history working with the National Park
Service." Critics took to the park's social media pointing out that the Blackstone company Tallgrass
is also funding a project that will power Google's large-scale AI data center in Cheyenne. Wank says
park funds shouldn't come with strings attached and for now, trust that the money was vetted
beforehand. For NPR News, I'm Jenna McMurtry in Jackson Hole. The opening night rosters in the NBA
have been turned in and there are 125 international players from a record-tying 43 countries. That
includes 17 French players like Victor Webagnama of the San Antonio Spurs, the most of any country
besides the US. This is NPR. This message comes from Aura. A data breach may have exposed more
than 153 million driver's licenses in the US. A breach like that doesn't wreck your life by
itself, but when someone uses your information, the cleanup becomes your job. That's what Aura
is for. Aura alerts you fast if your info shows up in a breach, then locks your credit and provides
US-based fraud support 24/7. You may not be able to stop all of it, but you can stop doing it alone.
